prompt: I remember reading a book in elementary school that I LOVED and I want to read it to my daughter. The problem is I can't remember the title. I know that when I first read it, it had recently won a Caldecott Medal. I have another memory from around the same time period of watching the Sydney Summer Olympics. All I remember about the plot is that it was based on a true story and set in the winter time. Can you help me remember the title?
answer:
The book may be **_Owl Moon_ by Jane Yolen, illustrated by John Schoenherr**.

It is set on a **winter night** and follows a child who goes owling with her father. The story is based on Yolen’s real experience taking her daughter owling, so it is often remembered as a true story. It won the **1988 Caldecott Medal**.

The Sydney Olympics were held in **2000**, so the timing may be slightly off—unless “recently” was a loose childhood memory—but _Owl Moon_ fits the winter, autobiographical, Caldecott-winning clues particularly well.
